_meta.title: Advanced Combat Resolution System v2
_meta.note: Formulas are given as readable pseudocode, not code. 'signature' is a derived stat computed from existing ship fields (see signatureSystem.derivation) so it works with ships that don't have an explicit signature field.
_meta.vocabulary: A round is one exchange inside a battle; a turn is the 24-hour clock a whole engagement fits inside (GamePlay/gameplay_specification.md 3). Names that count rounds say so (updatedRoundStructure, shotsPerRound, cooldownRounds, rechargeRatePerRound, regenPerRound); v1's turnStructure keeps its upstream name in data-template.json. turnRate and the turn penalty are about heading, not the clock.
_meta.rulings: The numbers the five rulings and the special-effect rules introduce live in tools/combat_tables.py; Combat-logic/combat_logic_specification.md 1.4, 2.1, 2.4, 2.5, 2.6, 3.4 and 3.7 explain them; tools/verify_combat.py holds the three together.

v1Overrides.description: Where this layer replaces a v1 term in data-template.json -> combatResolution. data-template.json is the upstream reference and is left untouched; read it through these overrides.
v1Overrides.retreatThreshold: v1 says hull < 15%. Ruled: hull at or below RETREAT_THRESHOLD (tools/gameplay_tables.py, 30%), matching both battle logs. GamePlay/conflict_specification.md 5 depends on it.
v1Overrides.sensorDebuff: v1's hitChanceFormula names a sensorDebuff it never defines. Ruled: it IS the sensorArray component critical, applied as a multiplier on preLockChance (see masterHitChanceFormula step 9). No second debuff exists.
v1Overrides.gunnerySkillAndComponentTargeting: v1's attacker.gunnerySkill/200 and the -0.2 component-targeting penalty both still apply; they are now written into masterHitChanceFormula steps 8a and 8b.

distanceSystem.description: Range is now the primary hit-chance driver. Each weapon still has optimal/maximum from its schema; this defines how hit chance decays between them.

bands.note: close-quarters bonus, but missiles risk not arming in time (see missileArmingRule)
cannot fire; must close distance or disengage

distanceSystem.missileArmingRule: Missiles fired at pointBlank (<10% optimal) have a 50% chance to fail to arm (treated as a clean miss) - they need travel time to arm warheads. This is the tradeoff for their long-range guidance advantage.

signatureSystem.description: Every ship emits a detectable 'signal' from mass, active systems, and power draw. Lower signature = harder to detect and lock, which suppresses incoming accuracy independent of raw evasion.

derivation.note: Bigger, higher-power, heavily-shielded ships are inherently loud. This is a starting point, not a fixed stat.

activeStateModifiers.effect: +8% signature per weapon volley fired (heat/EM bloom)
+40% signature (engine flare); topSpeed and acceleration x1.25 (R6, movementSystem)
-50% signature, but -30% topSpeed and weapons cannot fire that round (non-essential systems powered down)

detectionAndLockOn.effectiveDetectionRange: R9: effective(sensors.detectionRange) * (componentCurrentHP.sensorArray / sensorArray.maxHP, live from CombatantState) * effective(sensorArray.effectiveness) * clamp((targetSignature / 16) ^ 0.5, 0.25, 4.0). The original sensorArray HP x signature/100 gave lock ranges from 0.2 to 70,000. See combat_logic_specification.md 2.3.
detectionAndLockOn.rule: if distance <= effectiveDetectionRange: target is 'locked' and full accuracy formula applies. If distance > effectiveDetectionRange: target is 'unlocked' - attacker may still fire but suffers the blindFirePenalty below.
detectionAndLockOn.lockOnBuildUp: A newly-locked target starts at lockQuality = 0.5 and gains +0.25/round while continuously tracked (line of sight + in range), capping at 1.0 after 2 rounds. Breaking range/LoS or target using runningSilent resets lockQuality to 0.
detectionAndLockOn.blindFirePenalty: finalHitChance is multiplied by 0.25 and lockQuality is treated as 0.5 flat, representing firing at last-known position

movementSystem.description: R6 (combat_logic_specification.md 1.4). Every ship and mine field has a position on one engagement line, in the same units as weapon ranges; distance(a, b) = |position(a) - position(b)|. Numbers live in tools/combat_tables.py.
movementSystem.units: speed = distance per time unit, acceleration = speed per time unit, one round = ROUND_TIME = 4 time units. Calibrated on Sable/Ember rounds 1-2: EMBER's line (slowest hull 201) closes 3,400 -> 2,600 while SABLE holds; 201 x 4 = 804.
movementSystem.opening: Each side's first-lock range is the longest lock any of its ships has on any enemy ship with round-1 states. The side with the longer one chooses the opening distance between the other side's first-lock range and its own. Sides start on two points that far apart; each ship starts at the speed its round-1 intent asks for (0 for hold, else maxSpeed or its speedLimit).

intents.hold: brake toward speed 0, drifting along the current heading meanwhile
intents.close: head toward a target; stop at a standoff distance (default 0). Pursuit is close on a withdrawing ship.
intents.open: head away from a target; stop at a standoff distance (default none)
intents.withdraw: head for the own side's rear at full speed; the only way to disengage
intents.speedLimit: optional on every moving intent; formation keeping is the slowest hull's maxSpeed
intents.standoff: a ship that reaches its standoff keeps its speed and holds station; only hold gives speed up

perShip: Ships move one at a time in ascending initiative order; the highest initiative moves last.
maxSpeed = effective(topSpeed) x state factors: runningSilent 0.70, afterburner 1.25, emp_disable 0.70 (2 rounds), engines disabled/destroyed 0.30 (turnRate x0.30 too).
speedStep = effective(acceleration) x ROUND_TIME (x1.25 under afterburner).
v0 = min(speed, maxSpeed). If the intent's heading reverses the current one while v0 > 0: turnedThisRound = true and v0 *= (1 - turnPenalty).
v1 = v0 moved toward (hold ? 0 : min(maxSpeed, speedLimit)) by at most speedStep.
position += heading x min((v0 + v1) / 2 x ROUND_TIME, distance still needed to reach the standoff); speed = v1.
movementSystem.disengagement: A ship at or below RETREAT_THRESHOLD hull must withdraw from the next round; any ship may. At the end of a round a withdrawing ship that no enemy holds a lock on (signatureSystem.detectionAndLockOn) leaves the battle, retreated rather than destroyed. Posture avoid withdraws every hull from round 1. At ROUND_CAP every ship still present disengages.

speedEvasionSystem.description: Replaces the flat evasionRating lookup with a dynamic value driven by relative speed and the attacking weapon's tracking stat, so fast small ships dodge slow-tracking capital guns but get caught by high-tracking PD/energy weapons.

formula.relativeSpeedFactor: targetSpeed * (1 - turnPenalty). targetSpeed is the speed the target ended the movement phase with (movementSystem); turnPenalty = turnedThisRound ? 0.5 * (1 - min(effective(turnRate), 150) / 150) : 0, and turnedThisRound means the target reversed heading while under way this round.
formula.recalibration: R6: the original (relativeSpeedFactor - trackingCounter) / 250 gave 99% of catalogue hull-vs-weapon matchups the full 0.35, a 140-speed battleship against a railgun included. Tracking now counts x5 in speed units and each 100 speed of excess is +0.10; about 17% of matchups get nothing, 73% are graded and 10% saturate. tools/combat_tables.py TRACKING_SPEED_FACTOR, SPEED_EVASION_DIVISOR.

designIntent: High-tracking weapons (PD lasers, pulse lasers, small fast-firing guns) counter speed evasion well -> good vs corvettes/destroyers.

Low-tracking weapons (railguns, mass drivers, capital ion cannons) lose a lot of effective accuracy against fast targets -> capital ships want escorts or need the target to be locked/immobilized first.
This is why EMP disable (ion cannons) and engine-critical hits matter: strip the target's speed to strip its evasion.

kinetic.notes: Straight-line ballistics; full range/signature/evasion formula applies with no adjustments. Reliable, no special interaction.

energy.notes: Same as kinetic for hit resolution; differentiates on damage-vs-shield-resistance instead. Beam weapons (Beam Laser, Particle Lance) ignore speedEvasionBonus entirely (near-instant travel time) but keep full range falloff.

missile.notes: Missiles get +25% to base hit chance and only apply 50% of the target's effectiveEvasion (guided course correction). This is their core advantage. The cost is twofold: limited ammo (weaponSchema.ammo depletes and cannot be refilled outside dock) and a mandatory point-defense interception sub-phase (see missileResolutionPhase) that happens BEFORE the hit roll - a shot-down missile never rolls to hit at all.

mine.baseHitChanceModifier: n/a - mines do not roll to hit directly
mine.notes: Laid as a field against a chosen enemy ship. Without proximity_trigger the field is command-detonated against that ship only; with it, the field fires on ANY ship, friend or foe, inside its trigger radius. The field sits at the anchor's position on the engagement line when laid and never moves (R6). See tools/combat_tables.py MINE_BASE and the proximity_trigger / area_denial rules.

melee.notes: Ruled: melee resolves as direct fire with no adjustments, like kinetic. Its range of a few dozen units means the attacker must be alongside: it declares a 'close' intent with a standoff inside the weapon's range.optimal (movementSystem, R6).

missileResolutionPhase.description: Runs as its own sub-phase, after the normal fire-resolution phase's targeting step but before damage is applied, for every missile weapon fired this round.
steps: 1. Volley size = min(weapon.fireRate.shotsPerRound, weapon.ammo). Decrement ammo by volley size immediately (spent whether they hit or not).
2. Missile arming check: apply missileArmingRule if launched at pointBlank range.

3. Only weapons carrying 'can_be_intercepted' enter this sub-phase. Defender's pool weapons (specialEffects contains 'point_defense', 'anti_missile' or 'anti_air', and assigned to the pool in targeting) each get shotsPerRound interception attempts this round, pooled across ALL incoming projectiles at the defending ship this round. A pool weapon may instead be assigned in targeting to cover one friendly ship within its own range.optimal (cover, spec 2.5): its attempts then join that ship's pool against missiles and craft alike, each multiplied by its own ship's pointDefenseBonus; out of reach they are lost for the round. 'point_defense' engages missiles and craft, 'anti_missile' missiles only, 'anti_air' craft only. A finite-ammo pool weapon spends 1 ammo per attempt.

4. For each interception attempt, roll against an incoming projectile (the defender allocates attempts until either attempts or projectiles run out): interceptChance = clamp(pdWeapon.accuracy.baseHitChance + pdWeapon.accuracy.tracking * trackingFactor / 150 + interceptChanceDelta - projectileEvasion, 0.05, 0.95). trackingFactor and interceptChanceDelta come from the pool weapon's own special effects (tools/combat_tables.py).

5. projectileEvasion base = 0.20. A HIGHER value is HARDER to intercept. Modifiers: 'high_tracking' on the missile +0.10; 'multi_hit' (swarm pods) +0.05 on each missile - and the SWARM also launches more missiles than a single PD mount can realistically cover, so volume overwhelms defense even if per-missile intercept odds are normal. (This step previously gave high_tracking -0.10, which made tracking missiles easier to intercept, contradicting its own note; the sign is corrected.)
6. Any missile successfully intercepted is destroyed and dealt with - no damage, no further rolls.
7. Any missile NOT intercepted (PD ran out of shots, or intercept roll failed) proceeds to the normal hit-chance formula using the missile weaponHitProfile (1.25x base, 50% evasion ignored).
8. If multiple missiles from the same volley hit, each rolls damage independently (they are separate warheads).
missileResolutionPhase.designIntent: This creates a rock-paper-scissors: missiles beat evasive/fast ships (ignore half their dodge), point-defense beats missiles (dedicated PD hardpoints shred small volleys), and swarm/saturation missile boats beat point-defense (more warheads than PD shots available). A ship with no PD hardpoints equipped is very vulnerable to any missile-armed opponent.

strikeCraftSystem.description: R7 (combat_logic_specification.md 2.6). Fighters and drones are craft, not weapons: no hardpoint, no range band, no lock of their own, and no direct-fire weapon can aim at one. Numbers live in tools/combat_tables.py CRAFT_PROFILES.
strikeCraftSystem.hangar: A ship carries floor(effective(aircraftCapacity)) fighters and floor(effective(droneCapacity)) drones: capacities.aircraft / capacities.drones plus the hangar modules' flat values. Craft fly in squadrons of up to SQUADRON_SIZE = 6, formed at launch.
strikeCraftSystem.cadence: Craft aboard at the start are stowed: fighters first launch in round 1 + 4, drones in round 1 + 1. A craft recovered in round r launches again from round r + 2 (fighters) or r + 1 (drones). Launch and recovery happen in the movement phase with no deck limit; a ship running silent does neither. A strike launches only at a ship its carrier holds a lock on.
strikeCraftSystem.movement: Squadrons move after every ship, at speed x ROUND_TIME a round (fighter 1,000 x effective(squadronSpeed); drone 600), with no acceleration or turn penalty, and stop at their destination. Intents: strike (attack on arrival; a fighter once, then return; a drone every round), escort (stay with a friendly ship; one anti_air attempt per craft per round against enemy craft), return (recovered on arrival).
strikeCraftSystem.interception: All craft attacking one ship in a round are one wave. It meets the target's own craft-engaging pool weapons (shared with missiles, missiles first by default), pool weapons other ships assigned to cover the target (spec 2.5 cover, within the weapon's range.optimal, shared with missiles) and the target's escorts, before any hit roll. Craft projectileEvasion = 1.10 x effective(squadronEvasion) for fighters, 1.00 for drones. area_denial downs one more craft of the wave per success.
strikeCraftSystem.attack: baseChance = baseHitChance x weaponHitProfiles[hitProfile].baseHitChanceModifier x accuracy (fighter 0.65, missile profile, x carrier.effective(squadronAccuracy); drone 0.70, kinetic profile, x controller.effective(weaponAccuracy)[drone], the Drones skill gate included), - 0.2 if a component is targeted. finalHitChance = clamp(baseChance - speedEvasion(target, tracking) x (1 - evasionIgnoredFraction) + target.effective(enemyHitChance), 0.05, 0.95). No range multiplier, no arming check, lockQuality 1. Damage: fighter 115 +- 15 explosive; drone 30 +- 4 kinetic x controller.effective(weaponDamage)[drone]. Critical chance 0.05 / 0.02.
strikeCraftSystem.losses: Interception is the only loss in flight. Drones die with their controller (destroyed or disengaged). A fighter whose carrier left recovers aboard any friendly ship with free aircraftCapacity, or is lost when the battle ends. Craft aboard a destroyed ship are lost with it. Losses carry into the next engagement; craft are restocked in turn phase 12 from manufactured resources, per craft.
strikeCraftSystem.mines: Decided with R7: when a mine layer is destroyed or disengages its command fields are spent and its proximity fields stay until they detonate, expire or are swept; every field expires when the engagement ends.

pseudocode: 1. Determine distance between attacker and target this round.
2. If distance > weapon.range.maximum: cannot fire, stop.
5. lockQuality = locked ? currentLockQuality (0.5 to 1.0, builds over rounds) : 0.5

8 (R8). baseChance *= attacker.effective(weaponAccuracy) for this weapon class - the Weaponry skill's x0.50 gate below level 5 lives here. Every stat below is read through effective(), combat_logic_specification.md 1.3.
8b. if targeting a specific component: baseChance -= 0.2   (carried forward from v1 componentTargetingRules)

9. preLockChance = baseChance * rangeMultiplier * lockQuality * componentAccuracyMultiplier, where componentAccuracyMultiplier is the product over the attacker's disabled or destroyed components of sensorArray 0.60 and bridge 0.50 (1.0 when both are intact). This is v1's sensorDebuff.
11. finalHitChance = clamp(preLockChance - effectiveEvasion + target.effective(enemyHitChance), 0.05, 0.95)   (R8: ECM, decoys and smoke make it negative)
12. NOTE: for weapons carrying 'can_be_intercepted', steps 1-11 only run on projectiles that survive missileResolutionPhase's interception step.

updatedRoundStructure: 1. Initiative: sort by initiativeScore = effective(sensors.initiative) + effective(crew.pilotSkill) / 5 + d20, descending (R8; v1's undefined 'sensorArray effectiveness' term is replaced by the initiative stat sensor modules already carry).

2. Signature/state declaration: each ship declares this round's state (normal / afterburner / runningSilent / shields up-down), which sets its signature per signatureSystem, and its movement intent (hold / close / open / withdraw, movementSystem). Carriers declare launches and squadron intents (strikeCraftSystem).
3. Detection phase: for every attacker-target pair, compute effectiveDetectionRange and update lockQuality (build, hold, or reset).
4. Power allocation phase: assign power across weapons/shields/engines.

5. Movement phase: every ship moves along the engagement line in ascending initiative order per movementSystem (R6), updating position, speed and every pairwise distance; proximity mine fields trigger here. Then craft launch, squadrons move and returning craft are recovered (strikeCraftSystem).
6. Targeting phase: each ship selects target(s) and weapon(s) to fire, constrained by range.maximum and ammo remaining.
7. Missile resolution sub-phase: run missileResolutionPhase for all missile weapons fired this round, and strikeCraftSystem.interception for every craft wave (ammo deduction + PD interception).

8. Direct-fire resolution phase: for all non-missile weapons, surviving missiles and surviving craft (strikeCraftSystem.attack), run masterHitChanceFormula, then apply damageFormula (shields -> armor -> hull/component) from the base combat system.
9. Critical checks on confirmed hits per componentCriticalTable.

10. End of round: shields recharge (if outside rechargeDelay window), signature bonuses from this round's actions expire, repair modules apply, check destruction/retreat; a withdrawing ship that no enemy holds a lock on disengages (R6).

workedExample.scenario: Destroyer 'Whisperfang' (topSpeed 309, evasionRating 0.23, shields up, no signature tricks) is targeted by Battleship 'Leviathan Crown' (gunnerySkill 74) at 1,900 with three of the weapons it actually carries: a low-tracking mass driver, an ion cannon, and a cruise missile bay.
workedExample.catalogueBacked: Every hull and weapon figure is the catalogue's (the named ships and wpn_064, wpn_155, wpn_200); tools/verify_combat.py recomputes each shot's finalHitChance from them. The first draft used an invented ion cannon and a 350/0.24 Whisperfang; its conclusion -- the capital gun at the 0.05 floor -- does not survive the real numbers.
workedExample.assumptions: Leviathan Crown's Weaponry skills at level 5 (accuracy multiplier 1.00); neither ship's module effects counted (combat_logic_specification.md 1.3's worked example shows what they add); the lock held long enough for lockQuality 1.0.
workedExample.lockNote: R9: Leviathan Crown (detectionRange 1150) holds Whisperfang (signature 53 x1.10 shields) out to ~2,204, so the lock at 1,900 holds.

massDriverShot.weapon: Voss Mass Driver Mk.1 (medium; base 0.62, tracking 8, optimal 1,508, maximum 3,016)
massDriverShot.interpretation: Tracking 8 covers 40 speed of the destroyer's 309; speed evasion takes 0.27 off a gun that would otherwise hit four times in five.

ionCannonShot.weapon: Ceridan Ion Cannon Mk.4 (large; base 0.81, tracking 26, optimal 1,815, maximum 3,358; emp_disable)
ionCannonShot.interpretation: Same battleship, same target, better tracking: 0.73. Its emp_disable hit then cuts the destroyer to 0.70 of its top speed for 2 rounds (spec 3.4), which takes its speed evasion away from the mass driver too.

cruiseMissileShot.weapon: Vanguard Cruise Missile Bay Mk.6 (capital; base 0.71, tracking 16, optimal 6,968)
cruiseMissileShot.rangeMultiplier: close band: 1,900 is 27% of optimal -> 1.00; above the 10% arming threshold
cruiseMissileShot.interceptionStep: Whisperfang carries no pool weapon (two coilguns and two mine dispensers), so nothing intercepts the volley: the missile reaches the hit roll at the 0.95 ceiling.
cruiseMissileShot.interpretation: A destroyer with no point defence is acutely vulnerable to missiles (PointDefenceReadout.undefendedAgainstMissiles). Its defence against a capital ship is not its speed but its signature: running silent, it is outside this lock entirely.
